title: midweek-gpu-throttle-investigation-and-prep-2026-06-18
content:
Attendees: Aisha Kumar (owner), Ethan Morales, Sofia Patel, Jonas Rivera, Priya Singh, Marta Lopez

Meeting type: mid-week deep-dive + ops prep (ad-hoc weekly collateral for the infra team)
Purpose: summarize investigation into mid-week GPU throttling events in EU-West-3, capture mitigations for next 72h, and align capacity planning for the rest of the month.

1) Summary of incident observed (last 48 hrs)
- Timeline: 2026-06-17 03:20 UTC -> 2026-06-17 09:40 UTC intermittent elevated latency for hosted-api text generation routes.
- Primary symptom: 95th p50 token latency spike from baseline ~180ms -> sustained ~540ms for ~3h windows, correlated with model variant h2-medium (H100 quantized) and long sequence workloads (>2048 tokens).
- Secondary symptoms: autoscaler increased dedicated H100 pool instances (burst policy) but many requests hit degraded throughput and errors 429/503 for canary routes.
- Observed thermal signals: node-level sensor logs show repeated short-duration thermal threshold crossings (Tjunction spikes on multiple H100 cards) followed by frequency/clock downscaling that looks like thermal protective throttling.

2) Root-cause hypotheses and evidence
- Hypothesis A: rack-level cooling imbalance in eu-west-3 AZ-b causing sustained junction temps on cards under mixed packing. Evidence: room-level HVAC logs show a ~7-minute cooling-loop blackout for 2 racks at 03:10 UTC; those racks hosted a disproportionate share of H100 nodes running heavy long-seq jobs.
- Hypothesis B: scheduler packing policy now bin-packing H100s to optimize utilization; workload colocation created thermal hotspots (dense long-seq jobs on neighboring GPUs). Evidence: scheduler trace + node placement show 72% of long-seq h2-medium tasks were placed on 3 racks.
- Hypothesis C: power/BIOS firmware regression that reduces fan curves under certain amp draw patterns. Evidence: BIOS change rolled to eu fleet three days ago (PR: infra/firmware-rollout#72) and recent node-level power telemetry shows slightly elevated PSU derating events on a subset of nodes.
- Conclusion: multi-factor. Primary immediate cause likely cooling/packing imbalance; firmware change may have lowered margin and made the effect visible.

3) Short-term mitigations executed during incident
- Emergency policy: temporarily switch long-seq heavy workloads to cold fallback model variant h2-small-quant (higher latency per-token but smaller memory/thermal footprint) — cut impacted 95th lat spike by ~60% for affected requests.
- Evacuated and rebalanced workload from two hottest racks to spare nodes in eu-west-3 and eu-central-1 (manual scheduler override).
- Rolled back BIOS fan-profile change for 12 effected nodes as a controlled rollback (PR id infra/firmware-rollout#72 -> reverted subset).
- Placed two racks into maintenance (drain) until HVAC vendor provides noise/pressure readouts.
- Opened a vendor ticket for on-site HVAC/PSU inspection (Vendor ticket: PD-1842).

4) Metrics and immediate impact snapshot
- Affected customer routes: 13 internal customer names (mostly PLG free-tier churn routes) and 4 paying dedicated tenants with fallbacks active.
- Estimated user-facing errors: ~1.1k 429/503 responses during window.
- Cost delta of mitigation (using fallback variants + extra node spin-up): +$3.2k for 24h window estimated.
- Fleet utilization change: H100 fleet utilization fell from 82% -> 59% after rebalancing; spare node pool temporarily drained to 14% reserve.

5) Medium-term actions (72h to 2 weeks)
- Action A: Run full thermal sweep and node-level fan profile validation across eu-west-3 racks; target complete by 2026-06-20. Owner: Jonas Rivera.
- Action B: Scheduler policy tweak: add thermal-aware placement heuristic to avoid bin-packing long-seq jobs on same rack for 7-day experimental window. Owner: Sofia Patel, due 2026-06-22.
- Action C: Expand preemptible H100-equivalent buffer in EU regions by provisioning 6 additional spare nodes (preemptible) to enable faster spillover for heavy requests. Owner: Ethan Morales, provisioning request raised 2026-06-18.
- Action D: Run controlled A/B of fallback model for long-seq 95th percentile to verify quality regression vs cost tradeoff (product/ML engagement required). Owner: Priya Singh (product), deadline 2026-06-25.
- Action E: Fleet firmware audit and rollback plan for recent BIOS/fan profile rollout; create runbook for staged rollbacks. Owner: Marta Lopez, due 2026-06-21.

6) Longer-term strategic items (30–90 days)
- Consider floor capacity reconfiguration for EU to shift 8 H100 equivalents from low-use regions to EU (cost vs latency trade analysis). Proposal draft due 2026-07-10. Owner: Aisha Kumar & finance modeling.
- Evaluate mixed-instance thermal-aware bin-packing algorithm as part of scheduler rewrite; include simulated annealing or ML cost model to predict thermal accumulation. Research spike requested: 3-week timebox. Owner: eng-research/applied-ml liaison.
- Cooling telemetry improvement: add per-rack pressure/airflow and per-node thermal gradient sensors ingestion into observability (dashboard + alerting). Scoped with observability team; budget discussion in next infra budget sync.

7) Communication and customer impact plan
- CS/Support notified that some tenants saw throttles; ticket triage in progress. Customer-facing incident note to be drafted by CS with input from infra (goal: short summary + mitigation + ETA for fix). Owner: Priya Singh to coordinate with CS.
- Internal Ops note: timeline and mitigation steps posted to #infra-ops Slack channel and pinned.

8) Open questions / unknowns
- Did the BIOS change only affect fan curve logic in EU nodes or is there a wider rollout schedule? (firmware team to confirm).
- What is the failure mode for preemptible nodes under heavy long-seq load — do they exhibit different thermal profiles? Need telemetry comparison.
- Can we reasonably keep fallback model as a short-term safety valve without degrading customer quality SLA? Product to advise.

9) Action-item checklist (compact)
- [ ] Jonas: full thermal sweep eu-west-3 racks (due 2026-06-20)
- [ ] Sofia: implement thermal-aware placement knob, startup experiment (due 2026-06-22)
- [ ] Ethan: provision 6 preemptible H100-equivalent nodes (request submitted 2026-06-18)
- [ ] Marta: firmware audit + rollback runbook (due 2026-06-21)
- [ ] Priya: coordinate customer incident note + A/B plan for fallback model (due 2026-06-25)
- [ ] Aisha: draft EU capacity reallocation proposal (due 2026-07-10)

10) Notes to self (informal)
- Keep emergency fallback route ready as automated playbook; today it was manual and involved multiple teams — we should codify sequence: detect -> model-fallback -> scheduler-evacuate -> billing adjustment.
- Look into adding a transient-thermal flag in our node-reporter telemetry so scheduler can see recent delta vs absolute temp.
- If HVAC vendor finds partial failure, schedule a 4-hour maintenance window during low-traffic window (suggest 2026-06-23 02:00–06:00 UTC).

Attachments and logs referenced in meeting: rack-sensor-logs-2026-06-17.csv (internal), scheduler-placement-trace-2026-06-17.log, telemetry-payload-sample.json, PR infra/firmware-rollout#72, JIRA INFRA-9273.

Next sync: ad-hoc follow-up Tuesday 2026-06-23 10:00 UTC or earlier if vendor confirms HVAC remediation.

Notes: This doc is a working log; will be copied to Confluence with sanitized customer IDs once incident postmortem is completed.
